content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a new SSL framework called MUlti-Granular Self-supervised learning (Mugs) framework to learn multi-granular visual features. Mugs includes 3 components: 1)an instance discrimination supervision (IDS) component, 2) a local-group discrimination supervision (LGDS) component, and 3) a group discrimination supervision (GDS) component. Experiments show marginal improvements over SOTA methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

+ A new component, LGDS, is proposed for SSL to distinguish a new category of features.

Weaknesses

- How can you show or verify that Mugs captures three granular features other methods can't? Is it possible other methods also capture these features but don't categorize them explicitly like Mugs does? Figure 4(a) only shows features are more concentrated and separated from each other. In this case, what is the impact to instance-level fine-grained feature learning?

-The novelty of this paper mainly is on the proposed local-group discrimination supervision (LGDS), where k is the key parameter for the KNN component. A low k will push LGDS towards GDS, and a high k will push LGDS towards IDS. In either case, LGDS becomes less effective. However, the choice of k is not sufficiently discussed or tested in the paper. The appendix says k=8 is used in the experiments. Why 8? Different k should be tried to show its impact.

- Why use the terms "teacher and student backbones"? Does the teacher branch perform better than student branch? What is the impact of stop gradient? It should be discussed.

-Experiment setup and results are not impressive as only ViT is tested and performance improvement is marginal over SOTA methods. Other common DNN architectures (e.g., MLP, CNN) should also be tested.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity

This paper is well organized.


Quality

The paper is technically solid in general.

Novelty

The novelty of this paper is low as the new idea is mainly on LGDS. Does LGDS discover new local-group features that are not extracted without LGDS or simply "It brings two local-group features y∗1 and y∗2 from the same image xe close"? If it is the latter case, LGDS generates a better representation, but these features can still be extracted by simply using GDS and IDS.

Reproducibility

Good.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presents a new SSL framework called MUlti-Granular Self-supervised learning (Mugs) framework to learn multi-granular visual features. The technical contribution and novelty of this paper is limited, and experiment setup is flawed.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposed a novel approach for multi-granular representation learning in self-supervised scenario. More specifically, existing self-supervised learning method network structure is good as some specific down-stream tasks, however, it is still challenging to output more general/robust representations which is powerful for more general/wide down-stream tasks. To this end, the proposed framework fully explores the distributions of the samples by three modules, including instance level, local-group level, and group level discrimination supervision strategies. In general, the method considers the sample distribution in these three different levels and aims to achieve more distinctive representations which achieve both fine and coarse power for downstream tasks.

Extensive experiments including baselines in different tasks, ablation studies, and multiple visualization results demonstrate the high performance of the proposed model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The background of self-supervised learning is comprehensively introduced, the motivation of the proposed multi-granular strategy is clear and reasonable. The three proposed modules are clearly introduced with reasonable/logical explanations, the modules are also clear to understand.

The experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model. Compared with the state-of-the-art approaches, the proposed model achieves the highest performance in most of the metrics.

There are wide range of experiments provided in this work which comprehensively introduce the characteristics of the proposed approach and each module. Specifically, the experiments including general down-stream tasks, t-SNE visualizations, case studies in various datasets.

Weaknesses:

InfoNCE loss are mainly deployed as the loss function to evaluate the differences between different instances/groups. Why is this loss function deployed? Are there any other loss functions also feasible for this setting? More introductions could be provided.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is clearly introduced the proposed method as well as each module. The strategy and module is easy to understand. Thus, the clarity and reproducibility should be good.

The proposed method utilizes three easy understanding and straightforward strategies to achieve good performance with comprehensive experimental results and analyses, to this end, the quality and novelty of the work is also good.
content.summary_of_the_review: In summary, this paper proposed a novel approach for self-supervised learning in more fine-grained scenario. The method mainly explores instance level, local level, and group level sample distribution to achieve this goal with three easy understanding modules and achieves good performance. To this end, the quality of the paper is good and I vote positive to this submission.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper considers self-supervised learning (SSL) by using three constraints: 1) instance discrimination supervision (IDS) which is the most common loss design in SSL, 2) local-group discrimination supervision (LGDS), and 3) group discrimination supervision (GDS). The objective is to impose multi-granularity information in SSL. The experiments on image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation shows that the proposed method is strong among the alternatives.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**

- Pretrained on ImageNet-1K, the results of this proposed method on ImageNet test is strong among the competitors. 

**Weakness**

- Understanding on existing methods are some over simplified. Conceptually, DINO and SwAV could be considered as hybrid of deep clustering and instance discrimination, provided that the last layer as a set of cluster centres. These cluster centres share the same concept of local group of this paper. There is no clear conceptual differences.

- Existing methods on SSL for dense downstream tasks (object detection and semantic segmentation) are overlooked, e.g., [A1, A2, A3], which consider additionally the level of region/parts in SSL (a different type of multi-granularity). 

- Writing is hard to understand and follow. For example, class token is misleading in SSL. The definition of local-group feature is confusing and no clear motivation.  Top-k neighbours are from the same instance or not? From the text, I feel the local group feature has some relation with mixup type of data augmentation, which is worthwhile to discuss (missing now).

- Experiments: 
> 1) The results on transfer learning scenario has less margin than those on ImageNet-1K (the pertaining dataset)
> 2) Ablation study: Table 8, where is the accuracy of 76.4% from for fully Mugs? It is not in any other table. This ablation is critical for studying the effect of each key constraint. 

**Refs**

[A1] Dai Z, Cai B, Lin Y, Chen J. Up-detr: Unsupervised pre-training for object detection with transformers. InProceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition 2021

[A2] Ziegler A, Asano YM. Self-Supervised Learning of Object Parts for Semantic Segmentation. InProceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition 2022

[A3] Xinlong Wang, Rufeng Zhang, Chunhua Shen, Tao Kong, and Lei Li. Dense contrastive learning for self-supervised visual pre-training. In CVPR 2021
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This proposed is a mix of previous SSL models with unclear and confusing writing, without significant novelty. The results are shown to be strong but hard to justify. The model is also some complex and seems not easy to reproduce. As such, the overall quality is weak.
content.summary_of_the_review: Conceptually, this work is limited in novelty as DINO and SwAV could be considered to model two levels of granularities (instance and cluster/group). The proposed method is some mix of existing SSL components, without significant novelty in design and concept. The writing up is also poor.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
